item.title: One hospitalised following Newtonforbes crash
item.description: One person was hospitalised following a three-vehicle crash in county Longford. The collision, which involved a bus and two parked cars, occurred shortly after 5pm on Monday in Newtownforbes. The occupant of one of the cars attended Mullingar Regional Hospital as a precaution. Advertisement No other injuries reported at this time. Investigations are ongoing.

item.title: Plans afoot to boost long-term housing
item.description: Plans to restrict short-term lets in towns with a population of more than 20 thousand are progressing. Agreement was reached within Government last night, marking a change from initial plans to target towns of 10 thousand people. item.title: Overcrowding continues at local hospitals
item.description: There were almost 70 admitted patients waiting for a bed at local hospitals this morning. That's according to the INMO's latest trolley watch report. Tuesday's figures show there were 52 patients waiting in Sligo University Hospital. Advertisement This included 33 in the emergency department and 19 on wards elsewhere. Meanwhile, there were 16 patients waiting in the Midland Regional Hospital in Mullingar.

item.title: Longford man pleads guilty to harassing female solicitor
item.description: A 54-year-old Longford man has pleaded guilty to harassing a female solicitor. Patrick Cassidy, of Dromard, Moyne, made the plea at Longford Circuit Court this afternoon. The charge related to harassing Pauline Brady between January 1, 2024, and January 7, 2025. Advertisement Judge Jonathan Dunphy thanked the jury for their time, and said their role in this case was finished. Cassidy will be sentenced on Friday.

item.title: Longford man jailed for 15 months for drugs and money-laundering offences - after nearly €28,000 in cash found in his home
item.description: A 37-year-old man has been jailed for 15 months for drugs and money-laundering offences, after almost €28,000 worth of cash was seized in his home in Longford town. The court heard he initially said most of the money was his mother-in-law's - and the rest was a deposit for a gravestone. At Longford Circuit Court today, Judge Jonathan Dunphy sentenced Martin McDonagh, from Congress Terrace in Longford town. item.title: Tefia Park remains sealed off
item.description: Tefia Park remains closed this closed this evening following a double stabbing in Longford town. Two men were left in a serious condition in hospital following the incidents which took place at around 9pm on Monday night. Gardaí sealed off an area close to the town’s Teffia Park estate after the incident. Advertisement Anyone who witnessed the incident is being asked to come forward. item.title: Deadly driver doubles speed limit
item.description: A motorist has been detected travelling at almost twice the legal speed limit during a routine operation by the Sligo- Leitrim Roads Policing Unit. Gardaí confirmed that the vehicle was recorded travelling at 113km/h in a 50km/h zone, a significant breach of road traffic regulations. During the same incident, the driver also attempted to overtake another vehicle at a junction, an action Gardaí described as dangerous and irresponsible. item.title: Popular local service station and shop sold
item.description: A popular local service station and shop have been sold. Walsh's, located in Smear, Aughnacliffe county Longford comprises of a well-established country store, a modern fuel forecourt, and an adjoining private residence. The transaction was handled by Smith Property, which confirmed that interest in the property was robust, driven by its strong commercial performance and flexible purchasing options.
